Automated Classroom Energy and Power Optimization 3
Abstract
Classrooms may consume electricity unnecessarily when lights, fans or air-conditioning, and projectors
remain ON while they are not required. This project proposes an IoT-based classroom energy and power
optimization system that uses an ESP32 microcontroller to monitor classroom conditions and support
automated device control. The planned inputs include two PIR motion sensors for presence detection, an
LDR for natural-light measurement, a DHT22 sensor for temperature and humidity, an RFID RC522 reader
for teacher authentication, and a PZEM-004T module for electrical measurements. Based on configured
rules, the ESP32 can operate a relay module connected to selected classroom loads. A web dashboard
and backend/database are proposed for viewing status, recording events, and reviewing energy readings
when those software components are integrated with the controller. The project also explores a Logistic
Regression model that uses PIR1 and PIR2 readings to estimate occupancy in two sections; this is the
current model described in the supplied notebook, not a validated final energy-saving result. The system is
intended to reduce avoidable electricity use while maintaining classroom comfort. Performance must be
evaluated through hardware tests, sensor readings, device-state logs, and measured energy data. No
measured energy savings or model accuracy is claimed in this document because verified experimental
results were not supplied.
Keywords: IoT, ESP32, smart classroom, energy optimization, PIR sensor, LDR, RFID, relay control,
occupancy prediction.
